ballots.rationale: The two anticipation frames are perceptually indistinguishable in preload, planted stance, weapon separation, and target-directed intent; neither establishes a credible superiority.

The left frame supplies a narrower blade but reads inside the target with a weak response, while the right frame supplies a stronger response but leaves a visible blade-to-target standoff; neither is clearer on the ballot's combined topology-and-causality criterion.
The left frame more clearly preserves the low same-direction weapon path and transmitted target recoil while maintaining planted braking with no overhead re-cock.
The right sequence gives the startup-to-impact phrase a clearer transmitted-force transition at the end of the shared acceleration arc.
The right sequence more clearly carries impulse through the opponent while the blade continues low into a readable brake.
Across real-time, quarter-speed, and focused beats, the right sequence has the stronger overall causal recoil and same-direction finish, although it remains far below the absolute reference bar.
